# vkernels — low-level CUDA kernels and communication primitives

`vkernels` is the kernel layer for [opentela](https://github.com/opentela-ai): hand-tuned
CUDA kernels and the communication primitives (collectives, overlap, topology) that sit
beside them. Everything ships with a **CPU reference implementation** so it can be unit-tested
and measured for coverage on machines **without a GPU**, and a CUDA implementation that is
compiled automatically when a CUDA toolkit is present.

## Layout

```
vkernels/
├── pyproject.toml            # Python project (src/python/vkernels), managed with uv
├── uv.lock                   #   `uv sync` installs the `vkl` CLI + deps
├── src/c/                     # C++/CUDA sources (the kernel library)
│   └── vkernels/
│       ├── util/             # Span, error/status, logging, build annotations
│       ├── core/             # device, stream, allocator abstractions
│       ├── kernels/          # low-level CUDA kernels, each with a CPU oracle
│       │   ├── elementwise/  #   add, scale, relu, …
│       │   ├── reduce/       #   block/grid reduction
│       │   └── gemm/         #   tiled SGEMM
│       └── comm/             # communication optimisation
│           ├── topology.{hpp,cpp}   #   rank/world/peer discovery
│           ├── channel.{hpp,cpp}    #   transport abstraction + mock backend
│           ├── allreduce.{hpp,cpp,cu}#  ring all-reduce
│           ├── overlap.{hpp,cpp}    #   compute/communication overlap
│           └── pipeline_boundary.{hpp,cpp,cu} # graph-capturable PP boundary (#10)
├── tests/                    # C++ unit tests mirroring src/c/ (100% line coverage target)
│   ├── python/               #   Python tests (vkl CLI + bindings)
│   └── third_party/minitest.hpp     # dependency-free test harness
├── meta/                     # build support: cmake, scripts, docker, benchmarks
│   ├── cmake/                #   CMake helpers (CUDA, coverage, sanitizers, testing)
│   ├── scripts/              #   build / test / coverage / format helpers
│   ├── docker/               #   Dockerfiles and profiling toolchain
│   └── benchmarks/           #   micro-benchmarks
├── src/                      # Language bindings
│   ├── python/               #   Python package: `vkl` CLI + kernel bindings
│   │   └── vkernels/
│   │       ├── cli/          #     argparse CLI (`list`, `info`)
│   │       ├── kernels.py    #     add/scale/relu/sum/max/gemm (public API)
│   │       ├── comm.py       #     topology/channels/allreduce/overlap/p2p
│   │       ├── core.py       #     Device/Stream
│   │       ├── _core.cpp     #     optional pybind11 backend (built by CMake)
│   │       └── _fallback.py  #     pure-Python reference (no build needed)
│   └── rust/                 #   Rust bindings (workspace: `vkernels-sys` FFI + `vkernels` safe API)
│       ├── vkernels-sys/     #     unsafe FFI; build.rs links the C++ library via CMake
│       └── vkernels/         #     safe `kernels`/`comm`/`core` API mirroring the Python one
├── src/c/vkernels/capi/       # C ABI shim (extern "C" + exception translation) for non-C++ consumers
├── docs/                     # architecture, kernels, communication, testing
└── .github/workflows/        # host (coverage) + CUDA CI
```

## Two-implementation model

Every kernel and collective in this repo is provided **twice**:

1. **CPU reference** (`*.cpp`) — always compiled, fully unit-tested, and treated as the
   correctness oracle. This is the code that is measured for 100% line coverage on host CI.
2. **CUDA implementation** (`*.cu`) — compiled only when `VKERNELS_BUILD_CUDA=ON` and a
   CUDA toolkit is found. GPU tests compare the CUDA path against the CPU reference.

This means you can develop, review, and get to 100% coverage on any laptop, and run the
GPU path only on machines that have a toolkit and device.

## Development environment (mise)

All language toolchains and build tools are pinned in [`.mise.toml`](.mise.toml) and
managed by [mise](https://github.com/jdx/mise). After installing mise, trust the
config and install the tools:

```bash
mise trust    # one-time: trust the repo-level .mise.toml
mise install  # fetch python 3.12, uv, cmake, rust, clang-format, …
```

mise ensures every developer (and CI) uses the same versions of the tools listed below.
It also provides tasks that mirror the Makefile — run `mise tasks` to see them.

| Tool | Pinned version | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `python` | 3.12 | pyproject.toml requires `>=3.9`; uv manages `.venv/` from this python |
| `uv` | latest | Python package manager (`uv sync`, `uv run`, …) |
| `cmake` | latest | Build system; CMakeLists.txt requires `>=3.18` |
| `rust` | latest | Optional Rust bindings under `src/rust/` (edition 2021) |
| `clang-format` | latest | Code formatter; also provides `clang-tidy` (shipped from LLVM) |
| `ccache` | latest | *Optional* — faster C++ recompilation |
| `ninja` | latest | *Optional* — alternative CMake generator |

CUDA and HIP toolkits are expected at the system level and are **not** pinned in
`.mise.toml`.

## Quick start

```bash
# One-time: install pinned tools
mise install

# Configure + build + test on the host (no GPU required)
cmake --preset host
cmake --build --preset host
ctest --preset host          # or: cmake --build --preset host --target test

# Line coverage (enforces 100% on code under src/c/)
# Or simply: mise run coverage
cmake --preset coverage
cmake --build --preset coverage
ctest --preset coverage
python3 meta/scripts/coverage.py --build-dir build/coverage --source-dir src/c --min 100
```

When a CUDA toolkit is available:

```bash
cmake --preset cuda          # enables VKERNELS_HAS_CUDA, compiles the .cu files
cmake --build --preset cuda
ctest --preset cuda
```

For GPU hosts that should not carry CUDA/NCCL development packages, build the
NVIDIA image instead. It contains the CUDA toolkit plus pinned NCCL runtime and
headers; the host only needs a compatible NVIDIA driver and NVIDIA Container
Toolkit:

```bash
docker build -t vkernels:cuda -f meta/docker/Dockerfile.nv .
docker run --rm --gpus all --ipc=host vkernels:cuda
```

Override `NCCL_PACKAGE_VERSION` at image build time when coordinating a CUDA or
NCCL upgrade. The image build fails if CMake does not detect NCCL.
To validate only the reusable CUDA/NCCL toolchain layer, build with
`--target toolchain`.

## vkl — listing the implemented kernels

`vkl` (Python, under `src/python/`) answers "what is implemented in this
repository?”. It scans the public headers under `src/c/vkernels/kernels/` and
`src/c/vkernels/comm/` and pairs each declaration with its implementations —
a `.cpp` CPU reference and/or a `.cu` CUDA file — so the list always
reflects the sources. No build step is required. The Python project is
managed with [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) from the root `pyproject.toml`:

```bash
uv sync                      # first time: create .venv, install deps + `vkl`
uv run vkl list              # kernels + comm primitives
uv run vkl list --kernels    # kernels only
uv run vkl list --comm --json   # machine-readable
uv run vkl info gemm         # details for one entry
uv run python -m vkernels.cli list   # equivalent (no console-script needed)
```

Or use the Makefile shortcuts (`make vkl ARGS=list`, `make py-test`,
`make py-sync`). Installing the package puts a `vkl` command on your PATH
(`uv sync` does this in editable mode; plain `pip install -e .` works too).
The repository root is auto-detected and can be overridden with `--root DIR`
or the `VKERNELS_ROOT` environment variable; `vkl --version` reports the
version from `src/c/vkernels/util/version.hpp`. See
`tests/python/test_discovery.py` for the exact discovery contract.

## Python bindings (opt-in)

Beyond the CLI, `src/python/vkernels/` exposes a documented Python interface to the
kernels and communication primitives themselves — `vkernels.kernels`
(add/scale/relu/sum/max/gemm), `vkernels.comm` (topology, channels, ring
all-reduce, compute/communication overlap, the p2p run-list gather) and
`vkernels.core` (Device, Stream). The interface dispatches to a compiled
pybind11 backend (`vkernels._core`, built from `src/python/vkernels/_core.cpp`
when `VKERNELS_BUILD_PYTHON=ON`) that calls the C++ library under `src/c/`,
and falls back to pure-Python reference implementations otherwise — so it
works with or without a build, and the two backends are cross-checked
bit-for-bit by the tests.

```bash
cmake --preset python        # host build + compiled backend + Python tests
cmake --build --preset python
ctest --preset python
uv run pytest                # or: make py-test

uv run python -c "from vkernels import kernels; print(kernels.add([1, 2], [3, 4]))"
```

See [`docs/python-bindings.md`](docs/python-bindings.md) for the full API.

See [`docs/architecture.md`](docs/architecture.md), [`docs/testing.md`](docs/testing.md),
and [`docs/communication.md`](docs/communication.md) for the design and conventions.

## Rust bindings (opt-in)

`src/rust/` is the Rust counterpart of the Python bindings: `vkernels-sys` links
the C++ library (built by CMake through the `cmake` crate; host-only by
default, `VKERNELS_RUST_CUDA=ON` for CUDA) via the C ABI in
`src/c/vkernels/capi/`, and `vkernels` wraps it in a safe, `Result`-based API
(`kernels`, `comm`, `core`). Build and test on any machine:

```bash
cargo test --manifest-path src/rust/Cargo.toml   # or: make rust-test
# or via the CMake preset (registers `rust_bindings` with CTest):
cmake --preset rust && cmake --build --preset rust && ctest --preset rust
```

See [`docs/rust-bindings.md`](docs/rust-bindings.md) for the full API.

## Status

Bootstrapped. The infrastructure (build, CUDA gating, testing, coverage, CI) is in place
and the reference implementations are wired up with passing, fully-covered tests.

### Kimi-K3 hybrid attention (issues #21, #29)

- **MLA** — Multi-head Latent Attention forward (absorbed form, online
  softmax), gfx942. See [`docs/kernels/mla.md`](docs/kernels/mla.md).
- **KDA** — the seven Kimi Delta Attention kernels (gated RMSNorm,
  gate chunk-cumsum, the gated delta-rule forward and its intra/inter/
  output sub-kernels, and bit-matrix packing), gfx942. The host reference
  is the cross-checked oracle; the device forward is a correctness-first
  cooperative recurrence. See [`docs/kernels/kda.md`](docs/kernels/kda.md).
- **bf16 GEMM** — tiled K16 bf16 MFMA GEMM for the K3 projection shapes.
  See [`docs/kernels/gemm_bf16.md`](docs/kernels/gemm_bf16.md).

A K3-shaped forward (MLA + KDA layers) runs on gfx942 and matches the
CPU/torch reference; `K3_DISABLE_KDA=1` is no longer required.

### GLM-5.3-Flash / DeepSeek-V3 sparse attention (issue #51)

- **DSA** — DeepseekSparseAttn sparse-MLA forward (absorbed form, online
  softmax, bf16-tolerant vs the CPU oracle). Replaces the tilelang
  `sparse_mla_fwd_decode_partial` (+`_combine`) decode kernels and the
  `_v1`/`_v2` prefill kernels, which GPU-fault on gfx942; the
  GLM-5.3-Flash `tail_dim == 0` shape tilelang cannot compile is a
  first-class, hand-checked case (the rope-tail dot is skipped at runtime).
  See [`docs/kernels/dsa.md`](docs/kernels/dsa.md).
- **MHC** — the two GLM-5.3-Flash / DeepSeek-V3 multi-head hybrid-attention
  pre/post kernels (`mhc_pre_gemm_sqrsum`, `mhc_post`) whose tilelang
  forms JIT-abort on gfx942 (dynamic shared > 64 KB non-optin cap). The
  HIP kernels use static shared memory sized to fit MI300A's non-optin
  cap (no `hipFuncSetAttribute` opt-in, no `hidden_block 256 -> 128`
  patch), bf16-tolerant vs the CPU oracle. See
  [`docs/kernels/mhc.md`](docs/kernels/mhc.md).

GLM-5.3-Flash serves on gfx942 with `--dsa-prefill-backend vkernels
--dsa-decode-backend vkernels` and no custom tilelang overlay.

# Build + benchmark dsa_kpool (issue #60) on an MI300A (gfx942) compute node.
# The kpool kernels are HIP/gfx942 (AMD) and run on CSCS beverin's `mi300`

#   sbatch -p mi300 -N1 --gres=gpu:1 --time=00:30:00 \
#     -o kpool_bench.%j.out meta/scripts/run_dsa_kpool_bench_mi300.sh
set -euo pipefail
: "${SRC:=$HOME/vkernels-60}"
B="$SRC/build_kpool"
mkdir -p "$B"

echo "=== node: $(hostname)  date: $(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ) ==="
rocm-smi --showproductname 2>/dev/null | grep -A1 "GPU\[0\]" | head -3
echo "=== lock perf level high ==="
rocm-smi --setperflevel high 2>/dev/null || echo "(setperflevel not permitted; continuing)"
rocm-smi --showclocks 2>/dev/null | grep -E "sclk|mclk" | head -4 || true

echo "=== configure (HIP, gfx942, Release, tests + benchmarks ON) ==="
cmake -S "$SRC" -B "$B" -DVKERNELS_BUILD_HIP=ON -DVKERNELS_BUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_HIP_ARCHITECTURES=gfx942 -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DVKERNELS_BUILD_BENCHMARKS=ON 2>&1 | tail -4

echo "=== build (vkernels + test_dsa_kpool_correct + dsa_kpool_bench + host oracle) ==="
cmake --build "$B" --target vkernels test_dsa_kpool_correct dsa_kpool_bench \
                                        vkernels_test_dsa_kpool -j 64 \
  2>&1 | grep -E "error:|Built target|dsa_kpool|kpool_correct" | tail -12

echo
echo "############ 1. HOST ORACLE (vkernels_test_dsa_kpool) ############"
"$B/tests/vkernels_test_dsa_kpool" 2>&1 | tail -6

echo
echo "############ 2. DEVICE CORRECTNESS (test_dsa_kpool_correct) ############"
"$B/meta/benchmarks/test_dsa_kpool_correct" 2>&1 | tail -24

echo
echo "############ 3. BENCHMARK (dsa_kpool_bench) ############"
"$B/meta/benchmarks/dsa_kpool_bench" 2>&1 | tail -64

echo
echo "===== DONE $(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ) ====="

# dsa-kpool — paged tail-cache pool compress/write (AMD gfx942, MI300A)

A latency + roofline characterization of the DSA kpool-cache kernels in
`src/c/vkernels/kernels/dsa_kpool.{cpp,hip}` (issue #60) — the bookkeeping
stage that maintains the **live tail** (a per-request ring of the most
recent tokens) and **compresses each completed pool** into the paged cache
for the DSA sparse attention path:

$$\text{out}[pool] = H_{128}\left(\frac{\sum_{p=0}^{P-1} \exp\!\big(s_p + ape[p] - \max_j (s_j + ape[j])\big)\, k_p}{\sum_{p=0}^{P-1} \exp\!\big(s_p + ape[p] - \max_j (s_j + ape[j])\big)}\right)$$

Two kernels, one warp-group (64 threads) per pool/request:

  * **`dsa_kpool_assemble`** (prefill) — gathers each pool's `pool_size`
    slots from the chunked cache + live tail, two-pass softmax-weighted
    mean over the pool, 128-point Hadamard, writes the compressed K into
    the paged pool slot.
  * **`dsa_kpool_decode_update`** (decode) — unconditionally writes the
    current token's key/score into the live-tail ring (in-place, masked
    no-op when the row is invalid); when the token closes the pool
    (`pos % pool_size == pool_size-1`) it compresses the complete pool
    into the paged out slot exactly like the prefill path.

Shapes follow GLM-5.3-Flash / DeepSeek-V3: `head_dim = 128` bf16 keys and
scores, fp32 `ape` positional gate, `pool_size ∈ {4, 8}`,
`tail_size ∈ {64, 128}`, `slots_per_page ∈ {8, 16}`.

## Correctness (on the bench node)

Host oracle 16/16; device-vs-oracle **14/14 PASS** (prefill 7, decode 7).
The compressed-K output carries only the bf16-store residual
(`max_rel ≈ 3.4e-3`, tolerance 2e-2, identical magnitude to the prefill
rows); the in-place live-tail update is an exact bf16 copy
(`max_rel = 0`).

Two harness bugs were found and fixed while benchmarking (see Caveats):
a device-side write-write race in the generated decode data, and vacuous
compress coverage (`out` was zero on both sides). The decode rows now
exercise both the compress and the tail-write paths.

## Prefill latency — `dsa_kpool_assemble` (1 warp-group/pool)

| n_pools | ps | tail | us(min) | us(med) | GB/s | AI | bound |
|--------:|---:|-----:|--------:|--------:|-----:|---:|-------|
| 1 | 4 | 64 | 10.71 | 10.71 | 0.41 | 1.5 | launch |
| 16 | 4 | 64 | 11.14 | 11.14 | 6.29 | 1.5 | launch |
| 64 | 4 | 64 | 11.19 | 11.20 | 25.0 | 1.5 | launch |
| 128 | 4 | 64 | 11.24 | 11.25 | 49.8 | 1.5 | launch |
| 256 | 4 | 64 | 13.69 | 13.69 | 81.8 | 1.5 | launch |
| 1 | 8 | 128 | 12.15 | 12.16 | 0.70 | 1.3 | launch |
| 64 | 8 | 128 | 12.66 | 12.66 | 42.8 | 1.3 | launch |
| 256 | 8 | 128 | 15.20 | 15.20 | 142.6 | 1.3 | launch |

## Decode latency — `dsa_kpool_decode_update` (1 warp-group/request)

| batch | ps | tail | us(min) | us(med) | GB/s | AI | bound |
|------:|---:|-----:|--------:|--------:|-----:|---:|-------|
| 1 | 4 | 64 | 11.68 | 11.69 | 0.42 | 1.4 | launch |
| 8 | 4 | 64 | 12.05 | 12.05 | 3.24 | 1.4 | launch |
| 32 | 4 | 64 | 12.11 | 12.11 | 12.9 | 1.4 | launch |
| 128 | 4 | 64 | 12.21 | 12.21 | 51.2 | 1.4 | launch |
| 256 | 4 | 64 | 14.49 | 14.49 | 86.2 | 1.4 | launch |
| 512 | 4 | 64 | 19.58 | 19.58 | 127.6 | 1.4 | launch |
| 1 | 8 | 128 | 13.54 | 13.55 | 0.66 | 1.3 | launch |
| 128 | 8 | 128 | 14.13 | 14.14 | 81.3 | 1.3 | launch |
| 512 | 8 | 128 | 21.47 | 21.47 | 214.0 | 1.3 | launch |

Roof: 1307 TFLOP/s bf16, 5300 GB/s HBM3, ridge ~247 FLOP/B.

## The binding constraint is LAUNCH/OCCUPANCY, not HBM or compute

  * **Arithmetic intensity 1.3–1.5 FLOP/B** — ~180× below the ~247 FLOP/B
    ridge; the kernel can never be compute- or HBM-bound at these shapes.
  * **Peak effective bandwidth 214 GB/s = 4.0% of the HBM roof** (bs=512,
    ps=8); peak 0.27 TFLOP/s = 0.02% of the compute roof.
  * **Latency is nearly flat from 1 to 128 warp-groups** (10.7 → 11.2 µs
    prefill; 11.7 → 12.2 µs decode): 128× more parallel work costs ~0.5 µs.
    The marginal cost beyond the floor is **~15 ns per request**; even at
    bs=512 the whole step is ~20 µs.
  * **Empty-kernel control**: a do-nothing 64-thread kernel launched
    back-to-back measures **2.8 µs/launch** on this node — so of the
    ~11 µs at bs=1, roughly a quarter is HIP dispatch and the rest is
    kernel execution under the dynamic clock (see caveat below). In
    serving terms the entire kpool step is 12–22 µs — noise against a
    ms-scale decode forward pass, and <1% of step time even if invoked
    per layer.

## Caveats and notes

  * **Timing methodology.** These kernels are sub-µs at small shapes;
    single-launch `hipEventElapsedTime` returns corrupted 0.0 ms on
    MI300A (dynamic-sclk domain change between configs + ~0.5 µs event
    resolution), which first showed up as `us=0.00, TFLOP/s=inf` rows.
    The bench therefore batches **2000 launches per timed sample** and
    divides (re-launching is idempotent: the compress reads slots other
    than the single live-tail write), with a warmup burst + sync before
    the first timed event and an implausibility retry, mirroring
    `bench_dsa_topk_logits.hip`.
  * **Clocks.** `rocm-smi --setperflevel high` is not permitted on this
    cluster; idle sclk was ~104 MHz. Batched launches keep the GPU busy
    but the governor's boost during the measurement is not pinned, so
    absolute µs are an upper bound; the flatness and per-request scaling
    are the robust signals.
  * **Harness race (fixed).** The decode test originally mapped several
    batch entries onto one request tail via `rpi[r] = r % n_reqs` with
    `pos[r] = r % sl[r]`; at batch=16 entries r=0 and r=8 both resolved
    to (req 0, phys 0) — a same-slot write-write race between two blocks
    that the serial CPU oracle cannot model (device result depended on
    block scheduling, failing ~90% of runs with `ts[r=2.91]`). Fixed by
    giving every valid entry its own tail (`n_reqs >= batch`), matching
    the real sglang contract of one decode entry per running request.
  * **Vacuous compress coverage (fixed).** With the original
    `pos[r] = r % sl[r]`, `slot` was never `pool_size-1` for a valid
    entry, so the decode compress output was never compared (both sides
    wrote nothing). Valid entries now alternate pool-closing / mid-pool,
    and `out` shows the expected ~3.4e-3 bf16 residual.
  * **Re-launch idempotence.** The batched timing relies on the decode
    kernel writing the live-tail slot that the compress never reads
    (`is_current` substitution), so repeating a launch on constant
    inputs reproduces the same state.

## Reproduce

```bash
# on a beverin mi300 node (gfx942):
rsync -a --exclude build* ./ beverin:vkernels-60/
sbatch -p mi300 -N1 --gres=gpu:1 --time=00:30:00 \
  -o kpool_bench.%j.out meta/scripts/run_dsa_kpool_bench_mi300.sh
# raw log of the run above: beverin-dsa-kpool-bench.log
```

## Journal

Benchmarked the issue-60 kpool kernels on CSCS beverin (MI300A, gfx942)
after bristen's idle GPU nodes proved unbootable. Getting a trustworthy
number took three fixes: (1) the first run printed `inf` TFLOP/s because
single-launch event timing cannot resolve a sub-µs kernel on MI300A —
switched to 2000-launch batched samples; (2) a node-dependent
correctness failure (bs=16 decode, `ts[r=2.91]`) looked like a kernel
bug but a 30-iteration argmax repro pinned it to a harness-generated
write-write race (two batch entries, same tail slot), fixed by making
the decode data respect the one-entry-per-request contract; (3) the same
repro revealed the decode compress path had never been checked at all
(`out` zero on both sides) — the harness now alternates pool-closing and
mid-pool entries. Final state: 14/14 device rows pass (5× repeat
verified), and the benchmark shows the kernels are launch/occupancy
bound bookkeeping ops — 12–22 µs per step at serving shapes, ~15 ns per
request marginal cost, 4% of the HBM roof at worst. Future work: pin
clocks if the cluster ever permits `setperflevel`, and re-measure the
dispatch floor on a quieter node.

# dsa — DeepseekSparseAttn sparse-MLA forward (gfx942 / MI300A)

The sparse multi-head-latent-attention forward of GLM-5.3-Flash /
DeepSeek-V3 (issue #51). An external *indexer* has already picked, per query
token, the top-`topk` most relevant KV tiles (`indices`); this kernel scores
each query against exactly those selected keys and produces the combined
attention output. It replaces the tilelang
`sparse_mla_fwd_decode_partial` (+`_combine`) decode kernels and the
`_v1`/`_v2` prefill kernels, which GPU-fault on gfx942 (the decode JIT fault
is the blocker this issue asks vkernels to close with gfx942 HIP kernels).
The shape tilelang *cannot even compile* — GLM-5.3-Flash
(`qk_rope_head_dim = 0` → `tail_dim = 0`) — is a first-class, hand-checked
case: when `tail_dim == 0` the rope-tail dot is skipped at runtime, so there
is no zero-size GEMM to lower.

- **Source (CPU)**: `src/c/vkernels/kernels/dsa.cpp`
- **Source (HIP)**: `src/c/vkernels/kernels/dsa.hip`
- **Header**: `src/c/vkernels/kernels/dsa.hpp`
- **C ABI**: `vk_dsa_config`, `vk_dsa_sparse_fwd` (host),
  `vk_hip_dsa_sparse_fwd` (device) in `src/c/vkernels/capi/`
- **Tests (host)**: `tests/kernels/attn/test_dsa.cpp` (10 cases, incl. a
  hand-checked `tail_dim == 0` GLM-5.3-Flash case and a `tail_dim > 0`
  DeepSeek-V3 case, plus a randomized matches-reference sweep over both
  shape families)
- **Tests (HIP)**: `meta/benchmarks/test_dsa_correct.hip` (device kernel vs
  `dsa_sparse_fwd_cpu`, bf16-tolerant, run on gfx942)
- **Benchmark**: `meta/benchmarks/bench_dsa.hip` (+ `bench_dsa.sh` driver)

---

## Per-token oracle

The math every kernel parallelises (verified by hand, the host oracle). For
query token `i`, head `h`, selected key index `idx = indices[i,0,k]` (masked
when `idx < 0` or `idx >= S_kv`):

```
d_v       = dim - tail_dim                      ( > 0; tail_dim may be 0 )
raw[i,h,k]   = q_main[i,h] · k_main[idx]
             + (tail_dim>0) q_tail[i,h] · k_tail[idx]
score[i,h,k] = sm_scale · raw[i,h,k]            ( sm_scale includes log2(e) )
w[i,h,k]     = 2^(score[i,h,k] - lse[i,h])      ( masked keys -> weight 0 )
out[i,h]     = Σ_k w[i,h,k] · v[idx]            ( d_v wide )
lse[i,h]     = log2( Σ_k 2^score[i,h,k] )        ( base-2, when return_lse )
```

`sm_scale = (1 / sqrt(dim + tail_dim)) · log2(e)`, so the weights are the
standard natural-exp softmax `exp(raw / sqrt(dim + tail_dim)) / Σ` expressed
in base-2 (FlashAttention's log2 trick). Masked keys contribute weight 0;
when *every* selected key is masked the output row is 0 and the LSE is
`-inf`. `kv_group == 1` (all heads share one key/value head); the
per-group `partial_o` / `partial_lse` the tilelang kernel emits are an
internal parallelism detail — the combined result is grouping-independent,
which the host test validates directly.

## Paged-MQA gated top-k logits (the kpool>1 indexer, issue #51)

The **first stage** that feeds the sparse-MLA forward above. The external
indexer computes, per query token and paged KV tile, a gated logit that the
subsequent top-k selects over (GLM-5.3-Flash `index_n_heads=32`,
`index_head_dim=128`, `block_size=64` hardcoded in deep_gemm). The
tilelang `deep_gemm.fp8_paged_mqa_logits` JIT-compiles on gfx942 but the
launched kernel **never returns** for `num_heads` in {32, 64}; this is the
portable replacement (host reference + HIP kernel).

For query batch `b`, KV token `t = i*block + j` (`i` in
`[0, ceildiv(seq_len[b], block))`, `j` in `[0, block)`):

```
out[b, t] = k_scale[ page[b,i], j ]
          * Sum_h ( max(0, Sum_d Q[b,h,d] * K[ page[b,i], j,d ] )
                    * gate[b, h] )
```

Tokens `t >= seq_len[b]` are **left unwritten** (exactly as the tilelang
path does with `clean_logits=False`: sglang's `topk_from_pooled_history_logits`
masks invalid positions via `group_lengths`/`topk_offsets`/`seq_lens` before
the top-k). The HIP caller and the unit test **zero the output first**
(strictly safer than the original's `new_empty`). `split_kv` is a
performance knob only — the grouped logit is grouping-independent (any
positive `split_kv` yields the same top-k), chosen as
`max(1, min(max_seq_len//block, NUM_CU//batch_size))` with `NUM_CU = 256`
(MI300A).

| Tensor | Shape | Dtype |
|---|---|---|
| `q` | `[bs, H, D]` | fp8 e4m3fnuz (device) / fp32 (oracle) |
| `kv` | `[num_blocks, block, D]` | fp8 e4m3fnuz / fp32 (`head_dim == 128`) |
| `k_scale` | `[num_blocks, block]` | fp32 (per-token scale; packed in the trailing `block*4` bytes of each KV block on the device path, passed separately on the CPU path) |
| `gate` | `[bs, H]` | fp32 (the indexer's `_get_logits_head_gate` weight, after `.squeeze(2)`) |
| `seq_lens` | `[bs]` | int32 (the pooled valid KV count) |
| `page_table` | `[bs, max_table_len]` | int32 (the pooled page table; `page_table[b,i]` indexes the `num_blocks` dim of `kv`/`k_scale`) |
| `out` | `[bs, max_seq_len]` (`max_seq_len = max_table_len * block`) | fp32 (zero first) |

- **Files**: `src/c/vkernels/kernels/dsa.{hpp,cpp,hip}`;
  `dsa_topk_logits_cpu` (host oracle, always compiled),
  `hip::dsa_topk_logits` (device, `VKERNELS_HAS_HIP`).
- **C ABI**: `vk_hip_dsa_topk_logits` (device only) in `src/c/vkernels/capi/`.
  There is no host `vk_dsa_topk_logits` — the host path *is* the CPU oracle,
  not the serving ABI. The FP8 e4m3fnuz dequant is folded into the load.

## Two-implementation model

Mirrors `mla.{hpp,cpp,hip}` from issue #21:

| Operation | CPU (`dsa.cpp`) | HIP (`dsa.hip`) |
|---|---|---|
| `sparse_mla_fwd_decode_partial` (+ combine) | `dsa_sparse_fwd_cpu` | `dsa_sparse_fwd` |
| `sparse_attention_fwd_kernel_v1/v2` (prefill) | `dsa_sparse_fwd_cpu` | `dsa_sparse_fwd` |
| tile selector | `dsa_config_for` | `dsa_config_for` (decode ≤8 q/block; prefill BQ q/block × 256 th) |

The CPU reference is a numerically-stable two-pass base-2 softmax, fp32
throughout (always compiled; the oracle on host CI). The HIP kernel is an
**online softmax**: each block owns one (query, head) pair — `bq` query rows
in prefill — streams its `topk` selected keys in `block_I` tiles repeated
`inner_iter` times, and accumulates the combined output directly in fp32
with bf16 storage. It matches the oracle to bf16 tolerance for both
`tail_dim == 0` and `tail_dim > 0`.

## C ABI

```c
// Per-shape tile selector (decode vs prefill).
int  vk_dsa_config(int S_q, int H, int dim, int topk,
                   int* bq, int* threads, int* block_I, int* inner_iter);

// Host entry: delegates to the CPU oracle.
int  vk_dsa_sparse_fwd(int S_q, int S_kv, int H, int dim, int tail_dim,
                       int topk, int kv_group, float sm_scale,
                       int return_lse,
                       const void* q, const void* kv, const void* indices,
                       void* out, void* lse);

// Device entry: dispatches the HIP kernel (gfx942). 0 on success, non-zero
// with a captured last-error string on validation failure.
int  vk_hip_dsa_sparse_fwd(int S_q, int S_kv, int H, int dim, int tail_dim,
                           int topk, int kv_group, float sm_scale,
                           int return_lse,
                           const void* q, const void* kv, const void* indices,
                           void* out, void* lse);

// Device-only: the paged-MQA gated top-k logits indexer (issue #51).
// `q_fp8`/`kvcache_u8` are fp8 e4m3fnuz; `weight`(gate)/`seq_lens`/
// `page_table` are fp32/int32. `out` is `[bs, max_table_len*block]` fp32
// (ZERO the output first; tokens >= seq_len[b] are left unwritten).
void vk_hip_dsa_topk_logits(int batch_size, int num_heads, int head_dim,
                            int block, int max_table_len, int max_seq_len,
                            int split_kv,
                            const void* q_fp8, const void* kvcache_u8,
                            const void* weight, const void* seq_lens,
                            const void* page_table, void* out);
```

`q`/`kv` are bf16; `indices` is int32 (padded to a multiple of 64; entries
`< 0` or `>= S_kv` are masked kpool tail tokens); `out` is bf16; `lse` is
fp32 and may be null when `return_lse` is false.

## Acceptance

* `vk_dsa_sparse_fwd` matches `dsa_sparse_fwd_cpu` within bf16 tolerance for
  both `tail_dim == 0` (GLM-5.3-Flash) and `tail_dim > 0` (DeepSeek-V3)
  shapes. The host tests are the oracle on host CI (no GPU available); the
  device kernel is validated on gfx942 against `dsa_sparse_fwd_cpu` by
  `test_dsa_correct.hip`.
* The GLM-5.3-Flash `tail_dim == 0` shape — which tilelang cannot compile —
  is served by the HIP kernel with no custom tilelang overlay.

## Benchmark (MI300A, gfx942)

`meta/benchmarks/bench_dsa.hip` (+ `bench_dsa.sh` driver). Roof: 1307
TFLOP/s bf16, 5300 GB/s HBM3, ridge ~247 FLOP/B.

The kernel scores `S_q · H · topk` (query·key) dots, each `W = dim + tail_dim`
wide (the key dot) plus `d_v = dim - tail_dim` wide (the value gather). At
the GLM-5.3-Flash decode shape (`dim = 256, tail_dim = 0, W = 256, d_v = 256,
topk ≤ 256`) the arithmetic intensity is `~2·(W+d_v)/(bytes/q + bytes/kv) ≈
0.25`, so the kernel is **memory-bound** on the index gather + key/value
reads — the target of a future tiled-key prefetch and partial-output
reduction. Numbers are collected on a gfx942 box via `bench_dsa.hip`.

# mhc — Multi-head hybrid-attention pre/post (gfx942 / MI300A)

Two of the tilelang MHC kernels from
`sglang/kernels/ops/layernorm/mhc.py` — the split-k
`mhc_pre_gemm_sqrsum` stage-0 kernel and the `mhc_post` combine — GPU-fault /
JIT-abort on gfx942 (MI300A, issue #51, part 2). `mhc_pre_gemm_sqrsum`
aborts JIT `init()` with *Requested dynamic shared memory 98304 exceeds
device limit 65536* because tilelang's HIP codegen never calls
`hipFuncSetAttribute` to opt in to the larger dynamic-shared cap (a per-stage
double-buffer pushes a 256-wide hidden block past MI300A's 64 KB *non-optin*
shared cap). The sglang-side workaround is to patch the kernel's
`hidden_block 256 -> 128`.

vkernels re-implements these two kernels as portable host references + HIP
kernels that run on gfx942 **without** that workaround: the HIP kernels use
*static* shared memory sized to fit MI300A's non-optin cap (no pipelined
double-buffer, no dynamic-shared request, no `hipFuncSetAttribute` opt-in).

The complex fused kernels (`mhc_pre_big_fuse` — RMSNorm + mix extraction +
Sinkhorn normalisation, and `mhc_fused_post_pre_fma`) remain on the
tilelang path; issue #51 accepts either this vkernels HIP MHC path **or** an
upstream tilelang `hipFuncSetAttribute` opt-in for them.

- **Source (CPU)**: `src/c/vkernels/kernels/mhc.cpp`
- **Source (HIP)**: `src/c/vkernels/kernels/mhc.hip`
- **Header**: `src/c/vkernels/kernels/mhc.hpp`
- **C ABI**: `vk_mhc_pre_gemm_sqrsum`, `vk_mhc_post` (host),
  `vk_hip_mhc_pre_gemm_sqrsum`, `vk_hip_mhc_post` (device) in
  `src/c/vkernels/capi/`
- **Tests (host)**: `tests/kernels/attn/test_mhc.cpp` (7 cases, incl. a
  hand-checked identity for `mhc_pre_gemm_sqrsum` over `hc_hidden_size` up
  to the static-smem limit, a hand-checked `mhc_post` identity, a
  zero-`a`-broadcasts-`c` case, plus randomized
  matches-`numpy`/`torch` sweeps for both kernels)
- **Tests (HIP)**: `meta/benchmarks/test_mhc_correct.hip` (device kernels vs
  `mhc_pre_gemm_sqrsum_cpu` / `mhc_post_cpu`, bf16-tolerant, run on
  gfx942)
- **Benchmark**: `meta/benchmarks/bench_mhc.hip`

---

## Per-token oracle

The math every kernel parallelises (verified by hand, the host oracle).

### `mhc_pre_gemm_sqrsum` — pre-norm GEMM + squared sum

```
hc_hidden_size = hc_mult * hidden_size          ( the per-token feature width )
hc_mult3       = hc_mult * (2 + hc_mult)        ( <= 32; the GEMM output width )

out[n, o]   = Σ_h  x[n, h] · fn[o, h]           ( o in [0, hc_mult3), h in [0, hc_hidden_size) )
sqrsum[n]   = Σ_h  x[n, h] · x[n, h]
```

`x` is `[num_tokens, hc_hidden_size]` bf16 on the device (fp32 on the host
oracle); `fn` is `[hc_mult3, hc_hidden_size]` fp32; `out` is
`[num_tokens, hc_mult3]` fp32; `sqrsum` is `[num_tokens]` fp32. The GEMM is
`x @ fn^T`; the squared sum is the per-token L2 energy of `x`. `out` must
not alias any input.

### `mhc_post` — post-attention combine

```
out[n, j, h] = c[n, j] · d[n, h]  +  Σ_{k=0}^{hc-1}  a[n, k, j] · b[n, k, h]
```

`a` (`comb_res_mix`) is `[num_tokens, hc, hc]` fp32; `b` (`residual`) is
`[num_tokens, hc, hidden]` bf16; `c` (`post_layer_mix`, squeezed over the
last axis) is `[num_tokens, hc]` fp32; `d` (`x`, the per-token input) is
`[num_tokens, hidden]` bf16; `out` is `[num_tokens, hc, hidden]` bf16. The
device kernel does a fp32 accumulation with a bf16 round-trip on storage —
the only divergence from the fp32 host oracle. `out` must not alias any
input.

## Two-implementation model

Mirrors `mla.{hpp,cpp,hip}` (issue #21) and `dsa.{hpp,cpp,hip}`:

| Operation | CPU (`mhc.cpp`) | HIP (`mhc.hip`) |
|---|---|---|
| `mhc_pre_gemm_sqrsum` (split-k stage 0) | `mhc_pre_gemm_sqrsum_cpu` | `mhc_pre_gemm_sqrsum` |
| `mhc_post` (post-attention combine) | `mhc_post_cpu` | `mhc_post` |

The CPU reference is fp32 throughout (always compiled; the oracle on host
CI). The HIP kernel is an online fp32 accumulator with bf16 storage:

- `mhc_pre_gemm_sqrsum` keeps a single static `hc_hidden_size`-wide bf16
  staging buffer in shared memory (<= 56 KB for the 28672-wide case), well
  within MI300A's 64 KB *non-optin* shared cap — so there is no
  dynamic-shared request and no `hipFuncSetAttribute` opt-in, the exact
  thing the tilelang codegen fails to emit. One block owns `hc_mult3`
  output columns (split across the `hc_hidden_size` accumulation with an
  inner tile), accumulating `out` and `sqrsum` in fp32 registers.
- `mhc_post` uses one block per `(token, output-head j)`, streaming the
  `hc` reduction over `k` and the `hidden` output over `h` with fp32
  accumulators, writing bf16 output.

Both match the oracle to bf16 tolerance.

## C ABI

```c
// Host entries: delegate to the CPU oracle. 0 on success, non-zero on
// validation failure.
int32_t vk_mhc_pre_gemm_sqrsum(int num_tokens, int hc_mult, int hidden_size,
                               const float* x, const float* fn,
                               float* out, float* sqrsum);

int32_t vk_mhc_post(int num_tokens, int hc, int hidden,
                    const float* a, const float* b, const float* c,
                    const float* d, float* out);

// Device entries: dispatch the HIP kernels (gfx942).
void vk_hip_mhc_pre_gemm_sqrsum(int num_tokens, int hc_mult3,
                                int hc_hidden_size,
                                const void* x, const void* fn,
                                void* out, void* sqrsum);

void vk_hip_mhc_post(int num_tokens, int hc, int hidden,
                     const void* a, const void* b, const void* c,
                     const void* d, void* out);
```

`x`/`b`/`d` are bf16; `fn`/`a`/`c` are fp32; `out`/`sqrsum` are fp32 for
`mhc_pre_gemm_sqrsum` and bf16 for `mhc_post`. The host C ABI takes fp32 for
every buffer (the bf16 round-trip is a device-only detail).

## Acceptance

* `vk_mhc_pre_gemm_sqrsum` and `vk_mhc_post` match the `mhc_*_cpu` oracle
  within bf16 tolerance. The host tests are the oracle on host CI (no GPU
  available); the device kernels are validated on gfx942 against the
  `mhc_*_cpu` oracle by `test_mhc_correct.hip`.
* The GLM-5.3-Flash shapes that the tilelang `mhc_pre_gemm_sqrsum` /
  `mhc_post` kernels cannot JIT (dynamic shared > 64 KB non-optin cap) are
  served by the HIP kernels with no `hidden_block 256 -> 128` patch and no
  custom tilelang overlay — the blocker issue #51 part 2 asks vkernels to
  close with gfx942 HIP kernels.

# dsa — DeepseekSparseAttn sparse-MLA forward (AMD gfx942, MI300A)

Latency + roofline characterization of the DSA sparse-MLA forward in
`src/c/vkernels/kernels/dsa.{cpp,hip}` (issue #51) — the second stage of
the GLM-5.3-Flash / DeepSeek-V3 sparse attention: an external indexer has
already picked, per query token, the top-`topk` KV entries (`indices`);
this kernel scores each query against exactly those keys and produces the
combined attention output:

$$\text{out}[i,h] = \sum_k 2^{\,\text{sm\_scale}\cdot q_{i,h}\cdot k_{\text{idx}_k} - \text{lse}_{i,h}} \; v_{\text{idx}_k}\qquad(\text{masked } \text{idx}_k \to w=0)$$

with `W = dim + tail_dim` (`tail_dim == 0` for GLM-5.3-Flash — the shape
tilelang cannot compile — and `tail_dim = 64` for DeepSeek-V3). Replaces
the tilelang `sparse_mla_fwd_decode_partial` (+`_combine`) decode kernels
and the `_v1`/`_v2` prefill kernels, which GPU-fault on gfx942, so there
is **no tilelang baseline delta measurable on this hardware**.

**Implementation under test** (see [`docs/kernels/dsa.md`](../../kernels/dsa.md)):
CPU fp32 two-pass oracle (`dsa_sparse_fwd_cpu`, always compiled) + HIP
online-softmax kernel — one block per `(BQ query rows, head)` pair,
streaming its `topk` selected keys one at a time in `block_I` tiles,
fp32 accumulation with bf16 storage, grid `(ceil(S_q/BQ), H)`; the bench
also sweeps `BQ` through `dsa_sparse_fwd_with_tile` (small autotuner).

## Correctness (on the bench node)

Device-vs-oracle **11/11 PASS** (GLM-5.3-Flash `tail_dim == 0` decode /
short / prefill, DeepSeek-V3 `tail_dim > 0`, plus two tiny hand-checked
shapes), `out` max_rel ≤ 3.9e-3 against a 2e-2 bf16 tolerance, LSE exact
to fp32. One harness fix was needed first (see Caveats): the tiny
`topk=2` hand-check shapes predated the issue-#59 launch-precondition
enforcement and aborted (`topk % (block_I*inner_iter)` with
`block_I=64`); they now pass `block_I = topk` (grouping is
result-independent).

## Workload

GLM-5.3-Flash (`dim=256, tail_dim=0 → W=256, d_v=256, H=64`) and
DeepSeek-V3 (`dim=576, tail_dim=64 → W=640, d_v=512, H=16`) shapes;
`S_q` sweeps decode → prefill, `topk` the indexer fan-out. Roof:
1307 TFLOP/s bf16, 5300 GB/s HBM3, ridge ≈ 247 FLOP/B.

## Results — `hip::dsa_sparse_fwd` (nid002664, 2026-09-08)

| 16 | 1 | 256 | 576 | 64 | 256 | 732.8 | 742.2 | 0.013 | 7.1 | 1.8 | mem | BQ=1 |
| 16 | 1 | 512 | 576 | 64 | 256 | 732.0 | 741.3 | 0.013 | 7.1 | 1.8 | mem | BQ=1 |
| 1 | 64 | 256 | 576 | 64 | 256 | 812.2 | 816.7 | 0.046 | 25.9 | 1.8 | mem | BQ=4 |
| 1 | 8192 | 1024 | 576 | 64 | 256 | 1832.8 | 1852.6 | 2.608 | 1463.7 | 1.8 | mem | BQ=4 |

Summary (README format; "baseline" = the tilelang kernels this replaces,
which fault on gfx942, so no delta is measurable on this node):

| Implementation | Time (ms) | Workload | Achieved GFLOPS | Delta to Baseline | Reproduce Script | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| tilelang `sparse_mla_fwd_*` | — | GLM-5.3-Flash decode | — | — | — | GPU-fault on gfx942 (the issue-#51 blocker); `tail_dim == 0` not even JIT-compilable |
| vkernels HIP `dsa_sparse_fwd` (BQ=1) | 3.125 | H=64, S_q=1, topk=2048, dim=256, tail=0 (decode, full topk) | 43 | n/a (baseline faults) | `meta/scripts/run_dsa_mhc_bench_mi300.sh` | full-topk decode |
| vkernels HIP `dsa_sparse_fwd` (BQ=1) | 0.397 | H=64, S_q=1, topk=256, dim=256, tail=0 (decode) | 42 | n/a | same | serving topk=256 |
| vkernels HIP `dsa_sparse_fwd` (BQ=1) | 0.203 | H=64, S_q=1, topk=128, dim=256, tail=0 (decode) | 41 | n/a | same | serving topk=128 |
| vkernels HIP `dsa_sparse_fwd` (BQ=4) | 0.492 | H=1, S_q=8192, topk=128, dim=256, tail=0 (prefill) | 2182 | n/a | same | 21% of HBM roof |
| vkernels HIP `dsa_sparse_fwd` (BQ=1) | 0.742 | H=16, S_q=1, topk=256, dim=576, tail=64 (DSv3 decode) | 13 | n/a | same | |
| vkernels HIP `dsa_sparse_fwd` (BQ=4) | 1.853 | H=1, S_q=8192, topk=256, dim=576, tail=64 (DSv3 prefill) | 2608 | n/a | same | 28% of HBM roof |

Autotuner (`dsa_sparse_fwd_with_tile`, us(med) per BQ): BQ=1 wins on all
decode shapes (3123.9 / 743.6 / 210.7 us); the long-prefill shape prefers
BQ=4 (488.4 us vs 508.0 at BQ=1). BQ has < 6% effect everywhere — the
kernel is not tile-shape bound.

## The decode binding constraint is OCCUPANCY / key-stream latency, not HBM

  * **Decode grids are tiny**: the launcher is `grid(ceil(S_q/BQ), H)` —
    the GLM-5.3-Flash decode shape runs **64 blocks on 228 CUs** (one
    per head), DSv3 decode **16 blocks**. Each block streams its `topk`
    keys strictly serially (one key per lane iteration, no double-buffered
    key tile), so per-block latency ≈ `topk` serial L2 round-trips.
  * **Effective bandwidth confirms it**: 21.5 GB/s at the full-topk
    decode shape is 0.4% of the HBM roof — but the entire kv working set
    (`topk·W·2 B` = 1 MB at topk=2048) is L2-resident, and the measured
    rate is ~0.3% of MI300A's L2 bandwidth too. The kernel is bound by
    in-flight memory parallelism, not by any roof.
  * **Serving takeaway**: per layer, GLM-5.3-Flash decode pays 0.20 ms
    (topk=128) / 0.40 ms (topk=256) / 3.12 ms (full topk=2048) for the
    sparse forward vs 0.2–0.9 ms for the indexer stage (see
    [`../dsa-topk/gfx942.md`](../dsa-topk/gfx942.md)); the forward
    dominates and scales linearly with `topk`.
  * **Prefill is closer to the roof** (21–28% of HBM at S_q=8192): more
    query blocks hide the key-stream latency; AI 1.8–2.0 FLOP/B is
    ~125× below the ridge, so this kernel family is memory-shaped by
    construction (each selected key is used once per head — the
    H-fold kv re-read is the structural cost the tiled-key/persistent
    follow-on must amortize).
  * **The follow-on levers**, in expected impact order: (1) split_kv for
    the forward — the same trick the indexer already ships (4.7× there,
    [`../dsa-topk/gfx942.md`](../dsa-topk/gfx942.md)) — to spread the
    `topk` stream over more CUs; (2) double-buffered key tiles to
    overlap loads with the online-softmax update; (3) an MFMA path for
    the Q·K dot (the indexer's mfma variant is the fastest there).

## Caveats and notes

  * **Clocks.** `rocm-smi --setperflevel high` is not permitted on this
    cluster; idle sclk was 95–96 MHz. Variance-driven iteration (median
    over ≥ 20 reps, CV < 3%) keeps the reported medians stable, but
    absolute µs are upper bounds; the roofline ratios and the topk/BQ
    scalings are the robust signals.
  * **Timing methodology.** `hipEventElapsedTime` around single launches;
    sub-µs rows print `<res` (below event resolution). All rows here are
    well above resolution except none — every dsa row is ≥ 200 µs.
  * **Tiny-shape harness fix (this run).** `test_dsa_correct.hip`'s two
    `topk=2` hand-check shapes predated the issue-#59 precondition
    enforcement (`topk % (block_I·inner_iter) == 0`) and aborted the
    whole binary with an uncaught `std::invalid_argument` — on main,
    since #59, the device gate has been unrunnable as written. Fixed by
    giving the tiny cases `block_I = topk` (tiling does not change the
    result); the nine service shapes are untouched.
  * **Same-build indexer numbers** are included in the raw log (section
    5): they match [`../dsa-topk/gfx942.md`](../dsa-topk/gfx942.md)
    within noise (mfma variant fastest, split_kv 4.7× at bs=1).
  * The WIP tree benchmarked here also carries the in-flight `fits_lds`
    cap-parameterization + wmma admission work (GB10 CUDA port); none of
    it touches the gfx942 forward path measured above.

## Reproduce

```bash
# on a beverin mi300 node (gfx942):
rsync -aC --exclude build* --exclude .git ./ beverin:vkernels/
srun --partition=mi300 -N1 -G1 --time=00:40:00 \
  bash meta/scripts/run_dsa_mhc_bench_mi300.sh
# raw log of the run above: beverin-dsa-bench.log
```

## Journal

Benchmarked the issue-#51 DSA sparse-MLA forward on CSCS beverin
(nid002664, MI300A) — the last GLM-5.3-Flash kernel group without perf
numbers. One blocker surfaced immediately: the device correctness gate
aborted on the tiny hand-check shapes because issue #59's precondition
enforcement (`topk % (block_I·inner_iter) == 0`) landed after the test
was written — a pre-existing main breakage, fixed by passing
`block_I = topk` for those two rows (the grouping is
result-independent). With the gate green (11/11), the benchmark exposes
a clear story: prefill runs at 21–28% of the HBM roof, but decode is
occupancy-bound — 64 blocks on 228 CUs streaming `topk` keys serially —
0.4% of the HBM roof and ~0.3% of L2 bandwidth, scaling linearly with
topk (0.20/0.40/3.12 ms at topk=128/256/2048 per layer). The BQ
autotuner confirms tiles are not the issue (< 6% spread). The highest-
leverage follow-on is split_kv for the forward (the indexer already
proved 4.7× from exactly that), then double-buffered key tiles and an
MFMA dot. The full stack now has measured numbers: indexer → kpool →
sparse fwd, plus MHC pre/post (see [`../mhc/gfx942.md`](../mhc/gfx942.md)).

# mhc — Multi-head hybrid-attention pre/post (AMD gfx942, MI300A)

Latency + roofline characterization of the two GLM-5.3-Flash /
DeepSeek-V3 MHC kernels in `src/c/vkernels/kernels/mhc.{cpp,hip}`
(issue #51 part 2) — the pre-attention stage-0 GEMM + squared-sum and the
post-attention combine, whose tilelang forms JIT-abort on gfx942 (dynamic
shared > 64 KB non-optin cap), so there is **no tilelang baseline delta
measurable on this hardware**.

$$\text{pre: } \text{out}[n,o] = \sum_h x[n,h]\,\text{fn}[o,h],\quad \text{sqrsum}[n] = \sum_h x[n,h]^2$$

$$\text{post: } \text{out}[n,j,h] = c[n,j]\,d[n,h] + \textstyle\sum_k a[n,k,j]\,b[n,k,h]$$

**Implementation under test** (see [`docs/kernels/mhc.md`](../../kernels/mhc.md)):
CPU fp32 oracles (always compiled) + HIP kernels using *static* shared
memory sized to fit MI300A's 64 KB non-optin cap (no
`hipFuncSetAttribute` opt-in, no `hidden_block 256 -> 128` patch):

  * `mhc_pre_gemm_sqrsum` — one block per **token** (`grid(num_tokens)`),
    the block's threads split the `hc_mult3` output columns, staging
    `x` once through a static bf16 shared buffer; fp32 accumulation of
    both `out` and `sqrsum`.
  * `mhc_post` — one block per `(token, output head j)`
    (`grid(num_tokens, hc)`), fp32 accumulators, bf16 store.

## Correctness (on the bench node)

Device-vs-oracle **11/11 PASS** (5 pre rows incl. the GLM-5.3
`hc_hidden=16384` and the wider `28672` branch, 6 post rows incl.
`hidden=4096/7168`): pre max_rel ≤ 2.0e-5 (fp32 storage), post max_rel
≤ 3.9e-3 (the documented bf16 round-trip residual).

## Workload

GLM-5.3 MHC shapes: `hc_mult=4, hidden=4096 → hc_hidden=16384,
hc_mult3=24` (decode `n=1` and a 7-token micro-batch) and the wider
`hidden=7168 → hc_hidden=28672` branch. Roof: 1307 TFLOP/s bf16,
5300 GB/s HBM3, ridge ≈ 247 FLOP/B.

## Results — `hip::mhc_pre_gemm_sqrsum` (nid002664, 2026-09-08)

| n | hc_hidden | hc_mult3 | us(min) | us(med) | TFLOP/s | GB/s | AI | bound |
|--:|----------:|---------:|--------:|--------:|--------:|-----:|---:|-------|
| 1 | 4 | 8 | 0.0 | 0.0 | <res | <res | 0.4 | mem |
| 1 | 16384 | 24 | 271.0 | 278.4 | 0.003 | 5.8 | 0.5 | mem |
| 7 | 16384 | 24 | 274.6 | 281.2 | 0.020 | 6.4 | 3.2 | mem |
| 1 | 28672 | 24 | 464.4 | 477.2 | 0.003 | 5.9 | 0.5 | mem |

## Results — `hip::mhc_post`

| n | hc | hidden | us(min) | us(med) | TFLOP/s | GB/s | AI | bound |
|--:|---:|-------:|--------:|--------:|--------:|-----:|---:|-------|
| 1 | 2 | 2 | 0.0 | 0.0 | <res | <res | 0.5 | mem |
| 1 | 4 | 4096 | 0.0 | 0.0 | <res | <res | 2.2 | mem |
| 7 | 4 | 4096 | 0.0 | 0.0 | <res | <res | 2.2 | mem |
| 1 | 4 | 7168 | 0.0 | 0.0 | <res | <res | 2.2 | mem |
| 4 | 8 | 1024 | 0.0 | 0.0 | <res | <res | 4.2 | mem |

Summary (README format):

| Implementation | Time (ms) | Workload | Achieved GFLOPS | Delta to Baseline | Reproduce Script | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| tilelang `mhc_pre_gemm_sqrsum` / `mhc_post` | — | GLM-5.3 MHC shapes | — | — | — | JIT-abort on gfx942 (dynamic shared > 64 KB non-optin cap; the issue-#51 part-2 blocker) |
| vkernels HIP `mhc_pre_gemm_sqrsum` | 0.278 | n=1, hc_mult=4, hidden=4096 (GLM-5.3 decode) | 3 | n/a (baseline faults) | `meta/scripts/run_dsa_mhc_bench_mi300.sh` | single-block at decode |
| vkernels HIP `mhc_pre_gemm_sqrsum` | 0.281 | n=7, hc_mult=4, hidden=4096 | 20 | n/a | same | ~flat vs n=1 |
| vkernels HIP `mhc_pre_gemm_sqrsum` | 0.477 | n=1, hc_mult=4, hidden=7168 | 3 | n/a | same | wider branch |
| vkernels HIP `mhc_post` | < 0.0005 | n=1..7, hc=4, hidden=4096/7168 | — | n/a | same | below event-timer resolution; negligible |

## The pre kernel is single-block-bound at decode; post is noise

  * **`mhc_pre_gemm_sqrsum` launches one block per token** — at decode
    (`n=1`) the entire GEMM runs on **1 of 228 CUs**, streaming the
    1.5 MB `fn` matrix through one block: 5.8 GB/s = 0.1% of the HBM
    roof (the working set is L2-resident; the block is latency-bound on
    the serial `hc_hidden` walk per output column, and the baseline
    re-streams `fn` per column un-coalesced — the tiled, swizzled-shared
    follow-on's target).
  * **n=7 costs the same as n=1** (281 vs 278 µs): the +6 blocks add
    parallelism for free; per-token marginal cost is ~0.4 µs once the
    one-block floor (≈ 270 µs) is amortized.
  * **Serving takeaway**: pre is ~0.28 ms per layer per decode step at
    GLM-5.3-Flash — comparable to the DSA indexer stage and worth a
    split-token/parallel-column redesign, but far below the sparse
    forward's decode cost (see [`../dsa/gfx942.md`](../dsa/gfx942.md)).
  * **`mhc_post` is below the event-timer floor at every serving shape**
    (< ~0.5 µs): with `hc=4, hidden=4096` the kernel moves ~0.5 MB in
    4 blocks — effectively free; no optimization warranted.

## Caveats and notes

  * **Clocks.** `rocm-smi --setperflevel high` is not permitted on this
    cluster; idle sclk was 95–96 MHz. Medians over ≥ 20 reps with CV <
    3% are stable, but absolute µs are upper bounds; ratios and scalings
    are the robust signals.
  * **`<res` rows.** Single-launch `hipEventElapsedTime` cannot resolve
    sub-µs kernels on MI300A (~0.5 µs event floor + dynamic-sclk domain
    changes); the `mhc_post` serving shapes and the n=1 tiny-control row
    print `<res`/0.0. If a precise post number is ever needed, batch
    2000 launches per sample as `bench_dsa_kpool.hip` does.
  * **The 28672-wide pre row runs within the static-smem budget** (56 KB
    < 64 KB non-optin cap) — this is the shape the tilelang path cannot
    even JIT; measured here with no `hidden_block 256 -> 128` patch.
  * Same-build caveat as the DSA doc: the WIP tree carries the in-flight
    GB10 CUDA-port refactor; the gfx942 MHC path is untouched by it.

## Reproduce

```bash
# on a beverin mi300 node (gfx942):
rsync -aC --exclude build* --exclude .git ./ beverin:vkernels/
srun --partition=mi300 -N1 -G1 --time=00:40:00 \
  bash meta/scripts/run_dsa_mhc_bench_mi300.sh
# raw log of the run above: beverin-mhc-bench.log
```

## Journal

Benchmarked the issue-#51 part-2 MHC pre/post kernels on CSCS beverin
(nid002664, MI300A) alongside the DSA forward (one shared run script,
`run_dsa_mhc_bench_mi300.sh`). Correctness was green on the first full
run (11/11) after the DSA-side tiny-shape fix. The numbers say: the
kernels are correct-but-underparallelized rather than kernel-bound —
pre launches one block per token, so decode GEMM work sits on a single
CU at 0.1% of the HBM roof (~278 µs/layer), while post is sub-µs and
effectively free. No tilelang baseline exists on gfx942 (JIT abort), so
the delta column is n/a by construction; the honest comparison is the
sglang-side alternative of patching tilelang's `hidden_block 256->128`,
which these HIP kernels make unnecessary. Future work: split the pre
kernel's output columns across more blocks (or batch tokens per block)
to lift the one-CU floor, and re-measure once the cluster permits
pinning clocks.

Done — we benchmarked the full GLM-5.3-Flash kernel stack on beverin (nid002664, MI300A/gfx942). Here's the summary:

## What ran
New script `meta/scripts/run_dsa_mhc_bench_mi300.sh` (patterned after the existing kpool one): syncs → builds on the `mi300` partition → runs correctness gates → `dsa_bench`, `mhc_bench`, plus `dsa_topk_logits_bench` for same-build consistency. Correctness: **DSA 11/11 PASS, MHC 11/11 PASS** vs the CPU oracles.

## Key numbers (medians)

**DSA sparse-MLA forward** — the headline finding is decode is **occupancy-bound, not roof-bound**:
| Shape | Latency | Achieved |
|---|---|---|
| GLM-5.3-Flash decode H=64, topk=128 / 256 / 2048 | 0.20 / 0.40 / **3.12 ms** per layer | 21 GB/s (0.4% of HBM roof) |
| GLM-5.3-Flash prefill S_q=8192 | 0.49 ms | 2.18 TFLOP/s, 1116 GB/s (21% roof) |
| DeepSeek-V3 decode / prefill | 0.74 / 1.85 ms | 7.1 GB/s / 1464 GB/s (28% roof) |

Decode launches only 64 blocks on 228 CUs (one per head) streaming `topk` keys serially — ~0.3% of even L2 bandwidth. The BQ autotuner confirms tiles don't matter (<6% spread). The highest-leverage follow-on is **split_kv for the forward** — the indexer stage already proved 4.7× from exactly that trick.

**MHC pre/post**: `mhc_pre_gemm_sqrsum` is one-block-per-token → ~278 µs/layer at decode on a single CU (5.8 GB/s), `mhc_post` is sub-µs (below event resolution) — negligible. No tilelang baseline exists on gfx942 (JIT aborts), so deltas are n/a by construction.

## Fixed along the way
- **Pre-existing main breakage**: `test_dsa_correct.hip`'s tiny `topk=2` shapes aborted after #59's precondition enforcement (`topk % (block_I·inner_iter) == 0`). Fixed by passing `block_I = topk` for those two rows — the device gate had been unrunnable since Sep 1.
- Stale `bench_dsa.sh` references in `docs/kernels/dsa.md` → now point at the real driver + perf doc.

## Artifacts
- `docs/performance/dsa/gfx942.md` + `beverin-dsa-bench.log`, `docs/performance/mhc/gfx942.md` + `beverin-mhc-bench.log` (following the perf-doc format, with caveats + journal entries)
- README now links both docs

Everything is left uncommitted alongside your in-flight GB10/WIP work for review — note the beverin run used your current WIP tree (verified: only `fits_lds` cap-parameterization, nothing touching the gfx942 paths measured).
how can we further improve this?

Looking at the measured gaps, here's where the leverage is, in order:

## 1. Kernel changes (the real wins)

**split_kv for `dsa_sparse_fwd` — the single biggest lever.** Decode runs 64 blocks on 228 CUs, one block per (query, head), each streaming `topk` keys serially. The indexer already proved this exact fix: 4.7× at bs=1 (897→195 µs). For the forward it's the same recipe the tilelang `decode_partial` + `_combine` pair used: emit partial `(out, lse)` per split, then a tiny combine kernel does the log-sum-exp merge (partial buffers are only `S_q·H·splits·(d_v+1)` fp32 — negligible). At the full-topk shape, split=64 turns 64 blocks into ~4096 → I'd expect the 3.12 ms to drop into the tens-of-µs range, and it removes the topk-linear decode penalty that currently dominates the serving step.

**Persistent/tiled-key kernel to amortize the H-fold kv re-read.** The structural cost: each key is re-read once per head. A block owning a 64-key tile (32 KB bf16, fits static smem) × a group of ~8 heads loops heads from shared memory — 8× fewer L2 streams, and combined with split_kv it composes. This is what the docstring's "tiled-key prefetch / persistent-kernel follow-on" refers to; double-buffering the tile hides the remaining latency.

**Un-single-block `mhc_pre_gemm_sqrsum`.** `grid(num_tokens)` puts decode on 1 of 228 CUs (278 µs, 0.1% of roof). Splitting the 24 output columns across blocks — `grid(num_tokens, hc_mult3)`, each block streaming one `fn` column coalesced — should be near-linear (~24×) down to ~12 µs, and fixes the un-coalesced `fn` re-stream the bench header already flags. `sqrsum` needs a one-block guard per token. `mhc_post` needs nothing; it's noise.

**fp8 kv input for the forward.** The #62 kpool work already ships an fp8e4m3+scale cache, but `dsa_sparse_fwd` only takes bf16. Halving kv traffic helps the HBM-bound prefill rows directly and halves the decode L2 streams too.

## 2. Benchmark methodology

- **Batched timing for sub-µs rows** — `mhc_post` prints `<res`; the kpool bench solved this with 2000-launch samples. Cheap to port so the tables have real numbers.
- **A real GPU baseline row.** "Delta to Baseline" is n/a because tilelang faults — but a naive torch baseline (gather indices → SDPA per query) runs fine on gfx942 and would make the delta column honest.
- **Wider autotuner**: only BQ is swept; `block_I`/`inner_iter` are free parameters the precondition already allows (anything dividing `topk`).

"""FlyDSL MLA decode launcher.  Uses aiter for device queries."""

import functools
import re
import shutil
import subprocess

import torch


def _gcn_arch_base(arch_name: str) -> str:
    """Strip target features (':sramecc+:xnack-') from a gcnArchName."""
    return arch_name.split(":", 1)[0]


@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=None)
def _get_lds_size_per_cu(arch: str) -> int:
    """Return the LDS (shared memory) size per CU in bytes for ``arch``.

    Cached per arch so a mixed-GPU process (or one that switches devices)
    gets the right LDS budget for the active device — not whichever GPU
    rocminfo happens to list first. Caller must pass the current device's
    base gcnArchName (e.g. ``"gfx942"``).

    Parses the GROUP segment pool size from ``rocminfo`` output, picking
    the first GPU agent whose name matches ``arch``.
    """
    rocminfo = shutil.which("rocminfo")
    if rocminfo is None:
        raise RuntimeError("rocminfo not found on PATH")
    result = subprocess.run([rocminfo], stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True)
    agents = re.split(r"Agent\s*\d+", result.stdout)
    for agent in agents:
        if "Device Type" not in agent or agent.find("GPU") == -1:
            continue
        # Match this agent's Name (e.g. "gfx942") against the requested arch.
        name_m = re.search(r"^\s*Name:\s*(\S+)", agent, re.MULTILINE)
        if not name_m or name_m.group(1) != arch:
            continue
        lines = agent.split("\n")
        for i, line in enumerate(lines):
            if re.search(r"Segment\s*:\s*GROUP", line) and i + 1 < len(lines):
                m = re.search(r"Size\s*:\s*(\d+)", lines[i + 1])
                if m:
                    return int(m.group(1)) * 1024  # KB -> bytes
    raise RuntimeError(f"No GPU GROUP segment found in rocminfo output for arch {arch!r}")

result.output:
# dsa — DeepseekSparseAttn sparse-MLA forward (AMD gfx942, MI300A)

Latency + roofline characterization of the DSA sparse-MLA forward in
`src/c/vkernels/kernels/dsa.{cpp,hip}` (issue #51) — the second stage of
the GLM-5.3-Flash / DeepSeek-V3 sparse attention: an external indexer has
already picked, per query token, the top-`topk` KV entries (`indices`);
this kernel scores each query against exactly those keys and produces the
combined attention output:

$$\text{out}[i,h] = \sum_k 2^{\,\text{sm\_scale}\cdot q_{i,h}\cdot k_{\text{idx}_k} - \text{lse}_{i,h}} \; v_{\text{idx}_k}\qquad(\text{masked } \text{idx}_k \to w=0)$$

with `W = dim + tail_dim` (`tail_dim == 0` for GLM-5.3-Flash — the shape
tilelang cannot compile — and `tail_dim = 64` for DeepSeek-V3). Replaces
the tilelang `sparse_mla_fwd_decode_partial` (+`_combine`) decode kernels
and the `_v1`/`_v2` prefill kernels, which GPU-fault on gfx942, so there
is **no tilelang baseline delta measurable on this hardware**.

**Implementation under test** (see [`docs/kernels/dsa.md`](../../kernels/dsa.md)):
CPU fp32 two-pass oracle (`dsa_sparse_fwd_cpu`, always compiled) + HIP
online-softmax kernel — one block per `(BQ query rows, head)` pair,
streaming its `topk` selected keys one at a time in `block_I` tiles,
fp32 accumulation with bf16 storage, grid `(ceil(S_q/BQ), H)`; the bench
also sweeps `BQ` through `dsa_sparse_fwd_with_tile` (small autotuner).

## Correctness (on the bench node)

Device-vs-oracle **11/11 PASS** (GLM-5.3-Flash `tail_dim == 0` decode /
short / prefill, DeepSeek-V3 `tail_dim > 0`, plus two tiny hand-checked
shapes), `out` max_rel ≤ 3.9e-3 against a 2e-2 bf16 tolerance, LSE exact
to fp32. One harness fix was needed first (see Caveats): the tiny
`topk=2` hand-check shapes predated the issue-#59 launch-precondition
enforcement and aborted (`topk % (block_I*inner_iter)` with
`block_I=64`); they now pass `block_I = topk` (grouping is
result-independent).

## Workload

GLM-5.3-Flash (`dim=256, tail_dim=0 → W=256, d_v=256, H=64`) and
DeepSeek-V3 (`dim=576, tail_dim=64 → W=640, d_v=512, H=16`) shapes;
`S_q` sweeps decode → prefill, `topk` the indexer fan-out. Roof:
1307 TFLOP/s bf16, 5300 GB/s HBM3, ridge ≈ 247 FLOP/B.

## Results — `hip::dsa_sparse_fwd` (nid002664, 2026-09-08)

Autotuner (`dsa_sparse_fwd_with_tile`, us(med) per BQ): BQ=1 wins on all
decode shapes (3123.9 / 743.6 / 210.7 us); the long-prefill shape prefers
BQ=4 (488.4 us vs 508.0 at BQ=1). BQ has < 6% effect everywhere — the
kernel is not tile-shape bound.

## The decode binding constraint is OCCUPANCY / key-stream latency, not HBM

  * **Decode grids are tiny**: the launcher is `grid(ceil(S_q/BQ), H)` —
    the GLM-5.3-Flash decode shape runs **64 blocks on 228 CUs** (one
    per head), DSv3 decode **16 blocks**. Each block streams its `topk`
    keys strictly serially (one key per lane iteration, no double-buffered
    key tile), so per-block latency ≈ `topk` serial L2 round-trips.
  * **Effective bandwidth confirms it**: 21.5 GB/s at the full-topk
    decode shape is 0.4% of the HBM roof — but the entire kv working set
    (`topk·W·2 B` = 1 MB at topk=2048) is L2-resident, and the measured
    rate is ~0.3% of MI300A's L2 bandwidth too. The kernel is bound by
    in-flight memory parallelism, not by any roof.
  * **Serving takeaway**: per layer, GLM-5.3-Flash decode pays 0.20 ms
    (topk=128) / 0.40 ms (topk=256) / 3.12 ms (full topk=2048) for the
    sparse forward vs 0.2–0.9 ms for the indexer stage (see
    [`../dsa-topk/gfx942.md`](../dsa-topk/gfx942.md)); the forward
    dominates and scales linearly with `topk`.
  * **Prefill is closer to the roof** (21–28% of HBM at S_q=8192): more
    query blocks hide the key-stream latency; AI 1.8–2.0 FLOP/B is
    ~125× below the ridge, so this kernel family is memory-shaped by
    construction (each selected key is used once per head — the
    H-fold kv re-read is the structural cost the tiled-key/persistent
    follow-on must amortize).
  * **The follow-on levers**, in expected impact order: (1) split_kv for
    the forward — the same trick the indexer already ships (4.7× there,
    [`../dsa-topk/gfx942.md`](../dsa-topk/gfx942.md)) — to spread the
    `topk` stream over more CUs; (2) double-buffered key tiles to
    overlap loads with the online-softmax update; (3) an MFMA path for
    the Q·K dot (the indexer's mfma variant is the fastest there).

## Caveats and notes

  * **Clocks.** `rocm-smi --setperflevel high` is not permitted on this
    cluster; idle sclk was 95–96 MHz. Variance-driven iteration (median
    over ≥ 20 reps, CV < 3%) keeps the reported medians stable, but
    absolute µs are upper bounds; the roofline ratios and the topk/BQ
    scalings are the robust signals.
  * **Timing methodology.** `hipEventElapsedTime` around single launches;
    sub-µs rows print `<res` (below event resolution). All rows here are
    well above resolution except none — every dsa row is ≥ 200 µs.
  * **Tiny-shape harness fix (this run).** `test_dsa_correct.hip`'s two
    `topk=2` hand-check shapes predated the issue-#59 precondition
    enforcement (`topk % (block_I·inner_iter) == 0`) and aborted the
    whole binary with an uncaught `std::invalid_argument` — on main,
    since #59, the device gate has been unrunnable as written. Fixed by
    giving the tiny cases `block_I = topk` (tiling does not change the
    result); the nine service shapes are untouched.
  * **Same-build indexer numbers** are included in the raw log (section
    5): they match [`../dsa-topk/gfx942.md`](../dsa-topk/gfx942.md)
    within noise (mfma variant fastest, split_kv 4.7× at bs=1).
  * The WIP tree benchmarked here also carries the in-flight `fits_lds`
    cap-parameterization + wmma admission work (GB10 CUDA port); none of
    it touches the gfx942 forward path measured above.

## Reproduce

```bash
# on a beverin mi300 node (gfx942):
rsync -aC --exclude build* --exclude .git ./ beverin:vkernels/
srun --partition=mi300 -N1 -G1 --time=00:40:00 \
  bash meta/scripts/run_dsa_mhc_bench_mi300.sh
# raw log of the run above: beverin-dsa-bench.log
```

## Journal

Benchmarked the issue-#51 DSA sparse-MLA forward on CSCS beverin
(nid002664, MI300A) — the last GLM-5.3-Flash kernel group without perf
numbers. One blocker surfaced immediately: the device correctness gate
aborted on the tiny hand-check shapes because issue #59's precondition
enforcement (`topk % (block_I·inner_iter) == 0`) landed after the test
was written — a pre-existing main breakage, fixed by passing
`block_I = topk` for those two rows (the grouping is
result-independent). With the gate green (11/11), the benchmark exposes
a clear story: prefill runs at 21–28% of the HBM roof, but decode is
occupancy-bound — 64 blocks on 228 CUs streaming `topk` keys serially —
0.4% of the HBM roof and ~0.3% of L2 bandwidth, scaling linearly with
topk (0.20/0.40/3.12 ms at topk=128/256/2048 per layer). The BQ
autotuner confirms tiles are not the issue (< 6% spread). The highest-
leverage follow-on is split_kv for the forward (the indexer already
proved 4.7× from exactly that), then double-buffered key tiles and an
MFMA dot. The full stack now has measured numbers: indexer → kpool →
sparse fwd, plus MHC pre/post (see [`../mhc/gfx942.md`](../mhc/gfx942.md)).

(`dsa_sparse_fwd_split_for`):

edits.newText:
The CPU reference is a numerically-stable two-pass base-2 softmax, fp32
throughout (always compiled; the oracle on host CI). The HIP kernel is an
**online softmax**: each block owns one (query, head) pair — `bq` query rows
in prefill — streams its `topk` selected keys in `block_I` tiles repeated
`inner_iter` times, and accumulates the combined output directly in fp32
with bf16 storage. It matches the oracle to bf16 tolerance for both
`tail_dim == 0` and `tail_dim > 0`.

### Split-key decode (`dsa_sparse_fwd_split`)

The plain forward's decode grid is `(S_q/BQ, H)` — 64 blocks on MI300A's
228 CUs at the GLM-5.3-Flash shape — so decode is bound by each block's
SERIAL key chain (~1.2 us per key: load→use, no pipelining), not by any
roof (0.4% of HBM at full topk). The split path (grid
`(ceil(S_q/BQ), H, split_kv)`) divides the per-query index range across
`split_kv` partial blocks, each writing its **normalized** fp32 partial
output (numerator / local row-sum — the flash-decoding convention) plus
the per-split lse, and a 64-thread combine kernel merges the splits in
the log2 domain (`w_s = 2^(lse_s − max)`, `out = Σ w_s·part_s / Σ w_s`,
`lse = max + log2 Σ w_s`; masked/empty splits carry lse = −inf and
weight 0). PERF ONLY — grouping-independent, verified against the same
oracle including uneven splits (`test_dsa_correct.hip` split rows).
`partial_out` (`S_q·H·split_kv·d_v` fp32) and `partial_lse
(S_q·H·split_kv` fp32) are caller-owned scratch; `split_kv == 1`
delegates to the plain kernel (null scratch allowed).

The recommended split comes from `dsa_sparse_fwd_split_for(S_q, H,
topk, block_I, num_cu)`: 1 for prefill (the plain grid already fills
the CUs), else `min(ceil(sqrt(2*topk)), topk)` for decode — fitted to
the measured sweep (`docs/performance/dsa/gfx942.md`): the optimum sits
at 8–32 keys per split (the serial chain, NOT CU filling, binds; the
indexer's floor formula is 5–6x off here), and the sqrt fit lands on
the measured best on all four decode shapes (20.0x at full topk).

edits.newText:
## FlyDSL (rocm/flydsl) — probe result: runs on gfx942, D=256 wrong, ours ~2.7x/byte faster

FlyDSL (ROCm's python-kernel DSL, the repo that now carries the
MLA/flash kernels tilelang could not compile) was probed on the same
node as a candidate missing-baseline source. Setup: `pip install
flydsl` (wheel 0.3.2, python3.11) + `torch 2.9.1+rocm6.3` + a repo
checkout for the `kernels/` package; the wheel's MLIR runtime links
`libamdhip64.so.7`, absent on this ROCm 6.3 node, so a compat symlink
(`libamdhip64.so.7 -> /opt/rocm-6.3.0/lib/libamdhip64.so.6`) is needed
(kernels launch and compute through it; a few benign
`hipErrorIllegalState` messages appear at warmup).

`flydsl_flash_attn_func` (gfx942 generic route, dense bf16) at the
GLM-5.3-Flash decode memory pattern (Sq=1, Skv=2048, H=64 — one q row
per head streaming all keys, structurally identical traffic to our
sparse forward at topk=2048 minus the gather):

| shape (dense) | med us | bytes | GB/s | output vs fp32 reference |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| H=64, D=128, Skv=2048 | 208 | 67 MB | 322 | **correct** (maxrel 0.005) |
| H=64, D=256, Skv=2048 | 218 | 134 MB | 615 | **WRONG** (maxrel 27) |
| H=8, D=256, Skv=2048 / H=16, D=256 / H=64, D=256, Skv=512 | ~ | ~ | ~ | **WRONG** (maxrel 11–30) — D=256 breaks regardless of H, Skv |
| H=64, D=576 (DSv3) | — | — | — | launch-time assertion (unsupported) |
| tiny (Sq=128, Skv=128, H=8, D=64) | 213 | — | — | correct; ~200 us DSL-runtime floor on small shapes |

Findings:

  * **Not usable as the DSA baseline.** It is dense-only (no topk-gather
    sparse kernel ships), and its gfx942 generic path is numerically
    broken at `head_dim == 256` — exactly GLM-5.3-Flash's shape — while
    D=128 verifies to bf16 tolerance. (Upstream bug, D=256-conditional,
    independent of H/Skv; worth filing.)
  * **But the perf signal validates the split-key work.** FlyDSL's
    compiler-tuned dense decode moves 67 MB in 208 us (322 GB/s); our
    split sparse kernel moves 134 MB (2x the bytes, D=256 + gather) in
    156 us (~860 GB/s true; the table's 430 GB/s uses the repo byte
    convention that counts the kv term once — see note). Same node, same
    pattern: **~2.7x more bandwidth per byte** than FlyDSL's flash
    codegen at the shapes that matter. Pre-split (3.12 ms), FlyDSL would
    have beaten our kernel by 14x — the gap was exactly the one the
    split path closed.
  * **Byte-model note (this doc).** The `GB/s` column above and in the
    tables counts kv bytes once per head per read-pass (repo-wide
    convention inherited from the original roofline script); FlyDSL's
    probe model counts K and V separately. The 430-vs-860 GB/s
    difference is bookkeeping, not physics — latency comparisons are
    model-free.
  * Remaining use: an authoring stack for future kernels (encodes the
    MFMA fragment layout at a higher level than our hand-written
    `gemm_bf16.hip`, autotunes, and its `mla_fwd_decode` fp8/MFMA
    decode-kernel design targets gfx950 MFMA — a candidate for the
    gfx950 port) — gated on the D=256 bug and the ROCm-7 wheel
    dependency being fixed.

Reproduce:

```bash
# on a beverin mi300 node (gfx942), after pip install flydsl torch (rocm6.3 index)
ln -sf /opt/rocm-6.3.0/lib/libamdhip64.so.6 ~/flydsl-compat/libamdhip64.so.7
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/rocm/flydsl.git ~/FlyDSL
srun --partition=mi300 -N1 -G1 bash -c 'PATH=$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH \
  PYTHONPATH=$HOME/FlyDSL LD_LIBRARY_PATH=$HOME/flydsl-compat python3.11 flydsl_probe.py'
```

# FlyDSL on gfx942 (beverin MI300A) — probed 2026-09-08

Assessment of https://github.com/rocm/flydsl as a candidate missing-baseline
source / authoring stack for the DSA sparse-MLA forward (the tilelang
kernels it replaces fault on gfx942, see
`docs/performance/dsa/gfx942.md` — FlyDSL section has the full tables).

## Setup on beverin (works, with one shim)

- `python3.11 -m pip install --user flydsl` (wheel **0.3.2**) — installs fine.
- `pip install torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/rocm6.3`
  (torch 2.9.1+rocm6.3; the default index gave a broken install).
- The wheel ships only the compiler; the kernels are repo-level Python:
  `git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/rocm/flydsl.git ~/FlyDSL`,
  `PYTHONPATH=~/FlyDSL`.
- **Wheel/runtime is built against ROCm 7** (`libamdhip64.so.7`), absent on
  the 6.3 node. Compat symlink works: `ln -sf
  /opt/rocm-6.3.0/lib/libamdhip64.so.6 ~/flydsl-compat/libamdhip64.so.7` +
  `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`. Kernels launch and compute through it (a few benign
  `hipErrorIllegalState` messages at warmup).

## Results (`flydsl_flash_attn_func`, gfx942 generic dense route, bf16)

At the GLM-5.3-Flash decode memory pattern (Sq=1, Skv=2048, H=64 — same
per-head key-stream traffic as our sparse forward at topk=2048):

- **D=128: correct** (maxrel 0.005 vs fp32 reference), 208 us, 322 GB/s.
- **D=256: WRONG** (maxrel 27 vs fp32 reference) — independent of H and
  Skv (H=8/16/64, Skv=512/2048 all wrong; D=128 all correct). Upstream
  bug candidate to file. D=576 (DeepSeek-V3): launch-time assertion.
- Small shapes carry a ~200 us DSL-runtime floor (irrelevant at serving).

## Verdict

1. **Not usable as the DSA baseline**: dense-only (no topk-gather sparse
   kernel ships) and its D=256 path — exactly GLM-5.3-Flash's head_dim —
   is numerically broken on gfx942.
2. **Validates the split-key decode work**: FlyDSL's compiler-tuned
   dense decode moves 67 MB in 208 us (322 GB/s); our
   `dsa_sparse_fwd_split` moves 134 MB in 156 us (~860 GB/s true) —
   ~2.7x/byte on the same node/pattern. Pre-split (3.12 ms) FlyDSL
   would have beaten our kernel 14x — exactly the gap the split closed.
3. **Future use**: authoring stack for the next round (encodes MFMA
   fragment layout above hand-written level, autotunes; its
   `mla_fwd_decode` fp8/MFMA decode design targets gfx950 MFMA) — gated
   on the D=256 bug + a ROCm-6.3-compatible wheel.

Byte-model note: the repo perf docs' GB/s columns count kv bytes once
per read-pass (repo convention); FlyDSL probes counted K and V
separately. Latency comparisons are model-free.

Related: [[dsa-topk-gfx942-perf]], [[glm53-flash-beverin-bringup-status]],
[[mi300a-dynamic-lds-no-optin]].

content.text:
Everything is verified and consistent. Here's the complete picture of what landed:

## Split-key decode — done and measured

**The implementation** (`dsa_sparse_fwd_split` + `dsa_sparse_fwd_split_for`, C ABI, host+device tests): the per-query `topk` range is divided across `split_kv` partial blocks (each writing its **normalized** fp32 partial + per-split lse), merged by a log2-domain combine — the flash-decoding scheme. One instructive bug along the way: weighting the *unnormalized* numerators gave exact LSE but outputs off by up to 11×; the correct weight applies to the *normalized* per-split output.

**The measured sweep rewrote the recommendation.** The indexer's CU-filling formula (recommended 3–4 at H=64) is 5–6× off: the binding constraint is each block's serial key chain (~1.2 µs/key load→use), so over-subscribing up to ~18 waves wins. The fitted formula `ceil(√(2·topk))` lands exactly on the measured best on all four decode shapes:

| shape | unsplit | split (`split_for`) | speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| GLM-5.3 decode, topk=2048 | 3.12 ms | **0.156 ms** (s=64) | **20.0×** |
| GLM-5.3 decode, topk=256 | 0.40 ms | **0.059 ms** (s=23→best 16) | 6.7× |
| GLM-5.3 decode, topk=128 | 0.20 ms | **0.045 ms** (s=16) | 4.5× |
| DSv3 decode, topk=256 | 0.74 ms | **0.094 ms** (s=23→best 16) | 7.9× |

17/17 device-vs-oracle (incl. uneven splits), `split_for` returns 1 for prefill, and the full ctest suite is **40/40 green** — including the python-bindings discovery contract, which needed my two new entries (and I caught a duplicate I'd introduced there). The bench harnesses now also discard the exact-0.0 event samples that caused the flaky `0.0 us / inf` rows.

**Serving effect:** the forward no longer dominates the indexer at any shape (0.045–0.156 ms vs the indexer's 0.2–0.9 ms) — the topk-linear decode penalty is gone.

## FlyDSL — probed empirically, not just surveyed

It installs and **runs on gfx942** (wheel 0.3.2 + torch-rocm6.3 + a `libamdhip64.so.7`→`.so.6` compat shim, kernels from a repo checkout). Three findings:

1. **Cannot be the DSA baseline**: dense-only, and its gfx942 generic path is **numerically wrong at D=256** (maxrel 27 vs fp32 reference — exactly GLM-5.3-Flash's head_dim, broken regardless of H/Skv; D=128 verifies cleanly; D=576 asserts at launch). Worth filing upstream.
2. **It validates the split work**: at the identical decode memory pattern, FlyDSL's compiler-tuned dense kernel moves 67 MB in 208 µs (322 GB/s) vs our split kernel's 134 MB in 156 µs (~860 GB/s true) — **~2.7× more bandwidth per byte for us**. Pre-split, FlyDSL would have beaten our kernel 14×; that was exactly the gap the split closed.
3. **Future use**: plausible authoring stack for the next round (MFMA fragment layout above hand-written level; its `mla_fwd_decode` targets gfx950 MFMA) — gated on the D=256 bug and a ROCm-6.3 wheel.

Docs updated: `docs/performance/dsa/gfx942.md` (split section + FlyDSL section + journal + refreshed raw log), `docs/kernels/dsa.md` (split-key section + ABI), README serving note, and a new KB note `flydsl-gfx942-assessment`. Remaining levers per the doc: double-buffered key tiles (now the top one), an MFMA dot, and batched-decode rows.
